newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares recover after slump, short covering.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares recover after slump, short covering.

text.p: Buying by domestic institutions and short covering lifted Bombay shares to positive territory at close on Tuesday from a morning tumble, brokers said.
They said the state-owned Life Insurance Corporation began hectic buying after the market dropped for the third straight trading session.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 26.19 points, or 0.87 percent, higher at a provisional 3,029.05 after sliding to 2,930.93 in early trade.
On Monday, the index had lost 98.41 points, or 3.17 percent, after plunging 153.46 points, or 4.71 percent, last week.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index closed 1.21 points, or 0.14 percent, lower at a provisional 872.79.
The 500-share CRISIL index gained 0.66 points to a provisional 582.92, off 571.20 day's low.
Analysts said the market, hurt by an economic slowdown and political uncertainties, lacked follow-up support that will make the recovery short-lived.
"One could expect some kind of correction but the market will stay down for some time," said Alok Sethi, director at Natwest Markets, the investment arm of National Westminister Bank Plc.
"We think there's still some way to go for a valuation of the market relative to interest rates," said Devina Mehra, director at broking firm First Global Investments.
She said she saw the benchmark BSE index sliding to 2,200-2,400 for a strong rebound to get going.
"That's the level when you could expect strong buying to come in .. a bull phase," she said.

SBI fell 8.0 rupees to 209.25, L&T 7.0 to 206, Bajaj Auto 6.50 to 873.50 and Indian Hotels 7.50 to 590.50. Hindustan Lever gained 14.50 rupees to 782.75, M&M 9.0 to 305.50, TELCO 9.75 to 404, MTNL 7.25 to 203 and Glaxo 8.50 to 196.
